scores.claim_text: Store count rolled 680 -> 665 with 12 opens and 27 closures; 665 stores across 3 nameplates, 243 owned / 340 leased / 79 ground-leased.
supports: C1.Q1: Bluemercury appears in 49 SEC filings (Macy's subsidiary listings every year — confirms brand exists)
C1.Q2: Simon Property Group's own 10-Ks mention 'Macy's' 12 times across 2018-2024 — strong landlord-counterparty corroboration of mall-anchor tenant relationship
scores.M_check: Counterparty mall-REIT discloses M as material tenant; subsidiary brands externally verifiable
scores.interpretation: Store-count trajectory is internally coherent: 680 + 12 - 27 = 665 reconciles to disclosed end-period total. Mall-REIT counterparty validation confirms tenant relationship. Structural store closures (27 in FY2025) signal continuing fleet contraction, but pace is moderate vs the multi-year transformation context — not yet a falsification trigger. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Capital structure: ~$6.0B operating leases primarily due after 2030; $2.4B long-term debt; senior unsecured notes $2,441M outstanding maturing 2027-2043; credit ratings split-rated (Moody's Ba1 / S&P BB+ / Fitch BBB-) with Stable outlooks across all three.
supports: C2.Q1: Macerich's 10-Ks mention Macy's 9 times across 2018-2023 — mall-REIT landlord counterparty confirms M as material tenant

C2.Q2: Only 2 EDGAR hits for 'going concern' in M's filings, both 2019-2020 credit-facility boilerplate language (not auditor opinion) — confirms NO going-concern qualifier (Layer 3 Rule 10 not triggered)
scores.M_check: Counterparty corroboration of long-tail lease exposure; absence of going-concern qualifier; rating-agency split
scores.interpretation: Layer 3 Rule 10 distress markers NOT triggered (no GC, no 25-NSE, no Form 15). However, the structural picture is mixed: two of three rating agencies hold sub-IG (Ba1/BB+) while M targets 'investment-grade credit metrics' as a capital-allocation goal — claim partially contradicted by current rating reality. Lease portfolio of $6.0B primarily due after 2030 is structurally back-loaded — Calibration Heuristic 12 flag (long-tail commitments). MODE: the going-concern test passes, but the IG-aspiration vs split-rating gap is a moderate-severity gap between management framing and external rating reality.

scores.claim_text: FY2025 comparable sales: total +1.5% (vs -0.9% FY2024, -6.0% FY2023); Macy's +0.4%, Reimagine 125 +1.0%, Bloomingdale's +7.4% (best in 14 quarters), Bluemercury +1.6% (20th consecutive quarter). Digital 35% of net sales. Net sales actually -2.4% due to ~$700M of FY2024-closed-store rollover.
supports: C3.Q1: 'Bloomingdale's' appears in 89 10-Ks (vast majority M's own subsidiary listings — brand well-established and externally visible)
Internal reconciliation: comp +1.5% with net sales -$529M = -2.4% reconciles via disclosed $700M store-closure rollover; gross margin only -40 bps (38.4% -> 38.0%) attributed to tariffs
scores.M_check: Comp claims tie to reported GAAP net sales with disclosed store-closure bridge; multiple consecutive periods of growth at luxury/Bluemercury
scores.M_value: Bloomingdale's brand verified; comp/net-sales bridge ties to within disclosed components
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 9 test (marketing comp vs financial-statement comp): comp +1.5% is presented BOTH in marketing-tier and consistent with MD&A reconciliation tying to net sales. No gap. Sequential improvement in three-year trajectory (-6.0% -> -0.9% -> +1.5%) is real. Bluemercury 20-quarter streak and Bloomingdale's 14-quarter high are specific and falsifiable. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Citibank Credit Card Program (sixth amendment Dec 2021) extends until March 31, 2030; credit card revenues $669M = 3.1% of net sales (up +25% from $537M in FY2024); proprietary penetration 40.1% (down from 41.6%); $328M interchange fee settlement in FY2025.
supports: C4.Q1: Capital One mentions Macy's 0 times in 10-K/10-Q (expected — COF is NOT the partner)
C4.Q2: American Express mentions Macy's 0 times (expected — AXP is NOT the partner)

Additional check: Citibank (CIK 0000831001) 10-K mentions Macy's 0 times — typical for card-issuer 10-Ks which aggregate retail-partner exposures; M's own filings reference 'Citibank' 40 times — partnership well-documented from M side
scores.M_check: Internal disclosure of Citi partnership at $669M; counterparty card-issuer 10-Ks aggregate so absence of named mention is non-falsifying
scores.M_value: M-Citibank own-mentions=40; counterparty Citi-named-Macy's=0 (expected per Heuristic 7 — card-issuer aggregation)
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 7 (counterparty disclosure threshold): card-issuer 10-Ks rarely name individual retail partners — they aggregate portfolio exposure. Absence is NOT a hard contradiction here. The +25% YoY jump in credit card revenues despite -1.5pp drop in proprietary penetration suggests one-time benefit (the interchange fee settlement?) or denominator/profit-share-tier shift, not pure organic. Worth flagging but not severe. The $328M interchange settlement is itemized separately, so the $132M jump in credit card revenues itself is meaningful. Program extends to 2030 — well beyond cutoff. PASS.

scores.claim_text: ABL Credit Facility REDUCED from $3,000M to $2,100M on April 9, 2025; maturity extended to April 2030; $0 outstanding. FY2025 debt actions: issued $500M of 7.375% senior unsecured notes due 2033; redeemed $393M + tendered $251M (cash cost $255M) + redeemed $194M August 2025; $33M extinguishment losses. Cash $1,246M (down from $1,306M).
supports: C5.Q1: 'covenant waiver' returns 0 hits across M's entire filing history — confirms NO covenant-waiver disclosures (Layer 3 Rule 10 distress marker NOT triggered)
$0 ABL borrowings + $1,957M capacity is liquidity-positive (no draw distress)
scores.M_check: Absence of covenant-waiver disclosures; ABL undrawn
scores.M_value: covenant waiver hits=0; ABL drawn=$0; cash=$1,246M
scores.interpretation: Two readings: (a) Bull — M proactively termed out at favorable maturity (2033 notes, 2030 ABL), ABL undrawn, no covenant issues — clean liability management; (b) Bear — 7.375% coupon on 2033 notes is structurally high (well above pre-2022 cost of capital); ABL reduced by $900M (30%) signals lender-side reduction in committed capacity, not just expense optimization. Two of three rating agencies maintain sub-IG (Moody's Ba1, S&P BB+). Cash declined $60M YoY. No going-concern, no covenant breach — Layer 3 Rule 10 clean. But the structural cost-of-debt and ABL haircut are MODE-level (moderate) concerns — these are real financing-cost headwinds even if not acute distress.

scores.claim_text: Macy's operates as a major department-store carrier of national apparel brands with $21.8B net sales and ~$3.6B merchandise purchase obligations (majority <1 year). By scale, M should appear as a material customer in apparel/consumer-brand 10-Ks.
supports: C6.Q2: Tapestry (TPR) 10-Ks mention Macy's only 3 times — all in 2018-2019 (same filing, different formats); ZERO mentions in 2020-2025 TPR 10-Ks
C6.Q3: VF Corp (VFC) 10-Ks mention Macy's 0 times
Additional: Levi Strauss (LEVI) 10-Ks mention Macy's 0 times
scores.M_check: Heuristic 7 — supplier 10-K named-customer disclosure crosses ~10% threshold for top customers
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 7 reading: ABSENCE across 4 major apparel suppliers indicates M is below the 'major-customer' disclosure threshold (typically 10% of supplier revenue) for HBI/VFC/LEVI/TPR. This is INFORMATIVE in two directions: (a) limited supplier-side concentration risk — M isn't propping up any single brand, BUT (b) M does not appear to be a category-defining wholesale anchor for these brands — its purchasing power may be lower than its brand profile suggests. The TPR pattern is most striking: mentions stop after 2019, consistent with TPR (Coach/Kate Spade/Stuart Weitzman) actively pivoting away from department-store distribution to DTC. This corroborates broader retail-secular pressure on department stores as a channel. MODE: soft cross-corroboration of secular channel erosion.

scores.claim_text: Opened new China Grove, NC fulfillment/store replenishment center — 2,650K sq ft (largest in network), leased, direct-to-customer, with automation/robotics/AI. FY2025 capex $740M; expected FY2026 ~$800M, focused on digital/tech/omni-channel.
supports: C7.Q1: 'China Grove' returns 22 cross-filer hits but all are unrelated (Vivakor, Dixie Group — China Grove is the NC town name referenced as address for other companies' operations); no external mention specifically tying to M's facility
Internal: facility appears in M's Properties Table with specific 2,650K sq ft Leased / DTC function — verifiable disclosure
scores.M_check: Facility listed in Properties table with specific square footage; capex level consistent with industry transformation peers
scores.M_value: China Grove appears in M's own Properties Table at 2,650K sq ft (largest in DTC network)
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational): the facility crosses from 'announced' to 'operational' — it's in the Properties Table at a specific square footage, not just narrative. Capex of $740M FY2025 / $800M FY2026 (~3.4% of net sales) is moderate for a retail transformation. No external counterparty mentioned the facility, but a leased DTC facility doesn't typically generate counterparty 10-K mentions. PASS.

scores.claim_text: FY2025 real estate gains $48M (down from $144M FY2024 and $61M FY2023); $107M net proceeds from asset dispositions. Impairment+restructuring $230M (vs $171M FY2024, $1,027M FY2023). Bold New Chapter is now in year 2 (announced Feb 2024).
supports: C8.Q1: 'Bold New Chapter' returns 46 hits, all in M's own filings — confirms internal branding launched Feb 27, 2024 (per first 8-K hit); plan announced -> now in operational year 2
Real estate gains trajectory: $61M (FY23) -> $144M (FY24) -> $48M (FY25) — non-linear, suggests monetization is opportunistic not programmatic; sharp YoY decline in FY2025
scores.M_check: Calibration Heuristic 3 stage-ladder: announced strategy (Feb 2024) crosses 2-year operational milestone; track named milestones
scores.M_value: BNC mentions=46 (all internal); RE gains trajectory $61M->$144M->$48M; impairments stayed elevated at $230M
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 3 stage-ladder application: 'Bold New Chapter' announced Feb 2024 is now in operational year 2. Three pillars (Reimagine 125 / Luxury / Simplify Operations) all have M-side evidence in MD&A: 125 stores reimagined (executed), China Grove opened (executed), Bloomingdale's/Bluemercury comps positive (operational). Plan-to-operational ladder is being met. BUT real-estate-gains dropped from $144M to $48M (-67%), suggesting easy monetization opportunities exhausted. Impairment-charge run-rate stays elevated ($230M FY2025) — Heuristic 11 store-count trajectory test signals continued fleet contraction beyond announcements. Recurring impairments + declining RE-gains + continuing store closures = the multi-year transformation is structurally extending, not finishing. MODE: announced milestones being hit on the visible pillars, but the operational tail (impairments, RE-gain decay) signals the plan is still consuming, not yet generating, durable operating leverage.
